questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Neeta said, "Let me see how Pragya performs in her preboard examinations."

options.text: Neeta wants to see Pragya's performance in her preboard examinations.
Neeta said that she wanted to see how Pragya performed in her preboard examinations.
Neeta wanted to see how Pragya would perform in her preboard examinations.
Neeta said I would see how Pragya performed in her preboard examinations.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Neeta said that she wanted to see how Pragya performed in her preboard examinations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

__
 
• The **given sentence** is a **direct speech**.
 
• The **basic rules** for changing or **converting direct speech into indirect speech**__**:**
 
 
• The **commas and inverted commas** are **removed **and '**that**' is **added**.
 
• The first person '**me**' will be changed into the third person '**she**'.
 
• "**Let **me" becomes '**wanted**'.
 
• The present simple tense format '**Subject + V1 (performs) + Object'** will be changed into the past simple tense format **'Subject + V2 (performed) + Object'.**
 
 
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as- **option 2*.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 

The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:

 
 

 
 
**Direct Speech**

 
 
 
**Indirect Speech**

 
 
 

 
 
Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)

 
 
 
Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)

 
 
 

 
 
Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)

 
 
 
Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)

 
 
 

 
 
Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)

 
 
 
Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)

 
 
 

 
 
Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)

 
 
 
Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)

 
 
 

 
 
Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)

 
 
 
Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)

 
 
 

 
 
Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)

 
 
 
Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)

 
 
 

 
 
Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

 
 
 
Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

questions.question:
**Directions: Four jumbled sentences are given. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. The minimum temperature in the national capital dropped yesterday as cold northwesterly winds continued to blow in from the hills.

B. North India has been witnessing a harsh winter this year.

C. However, experts said the minimum temperatures would increase over the next few days due to a cloud cover.

D. A favourable outcome of the wind factor was that there was a slight decrease in air pollution levels due to the wind speeds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BADC".**
​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about "North India". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
 
• The phrase "**minimum temperature**" in the sentence 'A' is linked with the 'harsh winter' mentioned in the sentence 'B'. Hence, 'A' follows 'B'.
 
• The phrase 'wind factor' mentioned in the sentence 'D' is linked with the 'winds' mentioned in the sentence 'A'. Hence, 'D' follows 'A'.
 
• The sentence 'C' is the concluding sentence. **Hence,** **the sentence** 'C'** is** the last sentence.**

 

After rearranging the sentences__: *North India has been witnessing a harsh winter this year. The minimum temperature in the national capital dropped yesterday as cold northwesterly winds continued to blow in from the hills. A favourable outcome of the wind factor was that there was a slight decrease in air pollution levels due to the wind speeds. However, experts said the minimum temperatures would increase over the next few days due to a cloud cover.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of a given sentence.**

We can buy diamonds, but we cannot buy sympathy.

options.text: Diamonds cannot be bought but sympathy cannot be brought.
Diamonds can be bought but sympathy cannot be bought.
Diamonds can be bought and sympathy cannot be brought.
Diamonds can be bought but sympathy can be brought.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Diamonds can be bought but sympathy cannot be brought**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** ​

 
• The given sentence is made up of two parts:
 
 
• ​We can buy diamonds
 
• We cannot buy sympathy
 
 
 
• ​Both the sentence use a **modal verb** '**can**'. The **structures for active/passive voices for modal verbs** are:
 
 
• **Active:** Subject + Modal verb + Verb (Ist form) + Object
 
• ​**Passive:** Object + Modal verb + be + Verb (IIIrd form) + by + Subject
 
 
 
• With the help of the above structures, we can convert the given sentences into passive voices:
 
 
• ​Diamonds can be bought
 
• Sympathy cannot be bought
 
 
 
• ​Now, if we combine these two sentences, the complete sentence would be:
 
 
• ***Diamonds can be bought but sympathy cannot be bought***.
 
 
 
• ​Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
